R5A-bear-walk-0003.name: 2.4 km E of Clatse Lake
R5A-bear-walk-0003.pressureWhy: 2.4 km on foot from the nearest parking (estimate).
R5A-bear-walk-0003.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2016 (10 years old), 30 m NE: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
SW facing slope, 16 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 60 m SW: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

seasonRows.notes: Bag 2; parts of MU 5-9 are closed to black bear hunting (Map F14, page 52) and the Mussel Inlet Special Management Area in MU 5-9 has no black bear season (page 43)

plan: Drive: from Old Bella Bella, about 31 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 52.29656, -127.83617, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 2.4 km E, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 250 m, about 72 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 5-9, Region 5. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-07, closures 2026-10-16.
R5A-bear-walk-0003.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 5-9: about 36 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.00 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: a long walk from parking. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

R5A-deer-drive-0001.name: By Mokst Lake
R5A-deer-drive-0001.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R5A-deer-drive-0001.parkWhat: pull off on Roscoe FSR (gravel road)

evidence.t: Mule deer winter range u-5-005 unit 14-91 (official), 250 m NE. Counts from October.
Cutblock harvested 2016 (10 years old), 720 m S.
Habitat zone Coastal Western Hemlock (CWHvm3): coast forest, where black tailed deer are among the most common large mammals (95%) and use logged ground often (80%) (lesson: Wet forests).
S facing slope, 15 degrees: sun melts snow first.

seasonRows.notes: LEH (Limited Entry Hunting): draw only, not a general open season
MU 5-9 is not listed in the Region 5 white tailed deer rows (my reading of the table).

plan: Drive: from Old Bella Bella, about 42 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 52.37631, -127.80096, pull off on Roscoe FSR (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 40 m NE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 9 m, about 5 min at 3 km/h.
Hunt: deer, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Watch the edge of the 2016 cutblock (720 m S) at first and last light. Sit above it with the wind in your face and glass (Tip).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 165 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 5-9, Region 5. Season: mule deer bucks Sept 10 to Nov 30 and more rows (synopsis page 44, 99%). 1 legal flag below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
